chun: Quick share — profiler + smoke canary show cluster OOMs are clustering around two things: kernel-selector fallbacks on long sequences and large contiguous KV slab allocations causing fragmentation. Dumping a short trace below.

chun: ```
E 03:12:47 cuda:0 OOM allocating 1.2GB (requested)
  allocator: failed to find contiguous slab of 1.6GB free
  backtrace: runtime::matmul_generic -> kernel_selector::choose -> infer::dispatch
```

alice: Ugh. Do we have the kernel-selector logs for the same window? need to know which kernels it picked when seq_len > 2048. Also what's current max_batch_tokens on canary?

ben: pushed a small config change to canary last night: lowered evict_ttl and forced periodic compaction. Command I used: `rdwctl apply --env=canary --set evict_ttl=30s,slab_compact_interval=60s`

ben: Canary metrics so far: OOMs -> 0 in last 1h (was ~6/h), but GPU mem fragmentation metric shows more frequent small free runs. latency p95 +3ms. Will watch. :eyes:

rafael: sharing hit-rate snapshot: https://graphs.internal/redwood/kv-hitrate?range=6h
rafael: TL;DR: after key-hash normalization change the steady-state hit-rate dropped 72% -> 44% for prompt prefixes > 512 tokens. looks like key canonicalization changed distribution across slabs.

sara: For immediate warmup we could prefill cold workers with the top-100 prefixes per customer after spin-up. small script: ```#!/bin/bash
for p in $(cat top_prefixes.txt); do
  curl -s -X POST "https://canary.api.redwood/v1/generate" -d "{\"prompt\": \"$p\", \"prefill\":true}" &
done
```

kv-agent-bot: [INFO] 2026-03-18T03:20:12Z KV compaction job started on canary pool (job_id=comp-20260318-0319)

chun: Key interaction I want to call out: our batching heuristic (max_batch_tokens) is tuned for throughput. Larger token batches push the kernel selector to pick high-throughput kernels that assume contiguous memory for KV caches. When fragmentation is high, allocation fails mid-batch and we hit OOM. So three levers: reduce batch token cap, improve compaction, or make kernel selector prefer memory-frag-friendly kernels for canary.

alice: Agreed. Short-term mitigation: cap max_batch_tokens per-device to 512 and enable slab_compact_interval=30s. Medium-term: add a fragmentation signal into kernel selector score.

ben: Ran quick canary with max_batch_tokens=512 + compact=30s. Results: OOMs gone, mean throughput -6%, latency stable-ish. I'll roll to 10% traffic if no regressions in 2h. deploy-bot: rollout started -> canary -> 10% (deploy/evict-compactness-20260318)

sara: Can someone upload the perf profiles (before/after) to bench repo and add a short regression test that replays the offending long prefixes? I can add the warmup script once we have it.

chun: Checklist for follow-ups:
- add fragmentation metric to runtime telemetry (ticket: runtime/telemetry)
- kernel-selector: add frag_score & config flag to prefer frag-friendly kernels
- bench: add replay test for long-prefix workloads + compare hit-rate deltas
- ops: opt-in prefill on container spin for canary (top prefixes per org)
- investigate key-hash normalization impact on slab distribution

alice: Nice. Please post short PR links here when ready. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
